title: Sweet potato weevil on sweet potato

Header: Sweet potato weevil on sweet potato

Prevention: III Use clean cuttings (cuttings that are not infested)
Avoid planting in the dry season
Prevent soil cracking, e.g. by mulching , ridging, routine irrigation
Incorporate green manure in soil, e.g.
Lantana camara and papaya leaves (repellent to sweet potato weevils)
Farm sanitation, e.g. brushing, weeding and removal of debris
Harvest promptly when tubers are mature
Conserve natural enemies such as spiders and ground beetles by avoiding to apply pesticides
Monitoring: Regular visit to farm to look for signs of infestation: eggs on leaves and vines; presence of the adult weevil on the stem and leaves
Damage is recognised by the holes in the vines or the tunnels in the tuber when you pull them up from the soil
For storage tubers that appear soft, smell, or with small darkened holes, cut open and look for tunnelling and larvae
Direct Control: Plants such as banana leaves can be used to transport predatory ants ( Tetramorium guineense ) to the sweet potato field
Re-ridge, earthen exposed tubers properly before storing
Destroy affected tubers, e.g. by burning
Curing of store tubers by washing
Restrictions: Chemical pesticides are generally ineffective against the sweet potato weevil since the weevils are protected from pesticides by feeding inside the roots and stem.
MAFFS does not recommend the application of pesticide to control sweet potato weevil
